$comment: Native components that are compiled into the shipped application and therefore appear in NOTICE.
They are not in package-lock.json because they are not npm packages: MuPDF is downloaded as source,
hash-verified, and statically linked into native/mupdf-shim by scripts/provision/mupdf.mjs.
MuPDF's own version is NOT restated here. generateNotice.mjs imports MUPDF_VERSION from the
provisioning script, so the pin has one home and the NOTICE cannot claim a version nobody built.
The bundled list below is what the PROJECT REFERENCE GRAPH from libmupdf.vcxproj compiles,
taken from source-file paths only. Three earlier readings were each wrong, in both directions:
1. thirdparty/'s directory listing — over-declares. It ships sources for targets we do not
build (curl, freeglut, zint, zxing-cpp).
2. A list written by hand from the spike's prose — under-declares.
3. Any `thirdparty\X` mention in libmupdf.vcxproj — over-declares AND under-declares at once.
It matched AdditionalIncludeDirectories, which names thirdparty\openssl\include and
thirdparty\libarchive\include — directories the 1.28.0 tarball does not even contain — so
OpenSSL entered a licence notice for a library the build has never seen. And libmupdf.vcxproj
compiles only MuPDF's own source/**, so every bundled library arriving through a referenced
project was invisible: tesseract and leptonica are statically linked and were both missed.
Confirmed against the shipped 42 MB DLL: `?AVTessErrStream@tesseract@@` is present as a mangled
C++ type, and no OpenSSL banner, SSLeay string or EVP_ symbol appears anywhere in it.
It is a declaration rather than a scan because the source is only present on a machine that has
provisioned it, and a NOTICE generable only there would be generated rarely.
checkNativeComponents() in generateNotice.mjs parses the vcxproj whenever the source IS present,
so the declaration cannot drift from the build in silence — the native CI job is where that runs.

components.name: MuPDF
components.role: PDF parsing, rendering and writing engine. Statically linked into the shim.
$licences: Every entry names the FILE its terms were read from, inside the provisioned MuPDF source
tree, plus a marker string that must still appear in that file. checkLicenceSources() in
generateNotice.mjs verifies both whenever the source is present.
The path is the point. 'Read from each library's own licence file' was previously asserted in
prose and verifiable by nobody — a reader who doubted an entry had to dispute it rather than
check it. Two of the sixteen do not even have a licence file where a reader would look:
leptonica keeps it in leptonica-license.txt and libjpeg has no licence file at all, its terms
being a section of README. An unverifiable claim about those two is not a small thing.
The marker is what makes this catch an upstream RELICENSING rather than only a moved file. A
version bump that changes a component's terms breaks the marker and fails the build, which is
the whole risk: these libraries arrive inside someone else's tarball, so nobody here reviews
their licence changes at the moment they happen.
mujs is the entry that most needs this. Artifex positions MuJS publicly as AGPL-or-commercial,
and a developer reading this repository would reasonably expect that. The tree we actually
ship carries an ISC grant, and no file under thirdparty/mujs contains the words 'Affero' or
'GNU General Public' at all. The shipped grant governs — but naming the file and the version
turns that from a claim into something a reader checks in one command.
The zint entry needed checking rather than assuming, because zint is two things under one
name: its LICENSE records that in 2013 the BACKEND was relicensed to BSD expressly so it could
be linked into other products, while the frontends and the Qt4 backend stayed GPL.
libzxing.vcxproj compiles 101 files and every one is under thirdparty/zint/backend — no
frontend, no backend_qt, no backend_tcl. A GPL-2-only component would have been a genuine
conflict in an AGPL-3 project; this is not one.
FreeType is the one genuinely DUAL-licensed component, and a notice records the option TAKEN
rather than the options available — a downstream redistributor needs to know which terms bind
them, and for a dual licence that follows from our choice, not from the menu. We take the
FreeType License, so the file cited is FTL.TXT itself rather than the LICENSE.TXT that merely
describes the choice. FreeType's own text is explicit that the two are 'mutually exclusive'
and that 'you must choose one', and that the FTL is compatible with GPL-3 but NOT GPL-2 — so
the alternative, GPL-2-or-later, is the branch that could conflict with AGPL-3 depending on
how a redistributor versions it. FTL cannot.
The FTL's binding condition on a binary distribution is narrower and more specific than 'cite
FreeType': it requires a disclaimer stating the software is based in part on the work of the
FreeType Team, in the DISTRIBUTION documentation. Naming FreeType in a licence table does not
satisfy it, so the disclaimer is rendered verbatim by generateNotice.mjs, and the packaging
test asserts NOTICE reaches the installed application — a file in a source repository is not
distribution documentation.
Checked for the dual-licence shape across all sixteen, by scanning each licence file for
choice-of-licence wording rather than by recalling which projects are dual-licensed. FreeType
is the only one. The hits on extract and jbig2dec are AGPL's ordinary '(at your option) any
later version' clause, which is a version range and not a choice of terms; the hits on
harfbuzz and zint were build instructions in READMEs.
harfbuzz is a composite rather than a dual: its COPYING states the whole is 'Old MIT' and that
individual subdirectories may carry their own COPYING. That needs no choice from us — every
part binds at once — and it is recorded with that caveat named.

brotli.marker: Permission is hereby granted, free of charge

cmark-gfm.marker: Redistribution and use in source and binary forms

freetype.spdx: FreeType License (FTL) — the option taken, not merely offered
freetype.note: Dual-licensed FTL or GPL-2.0-or-later; the two are mutually exclusive and we take the FTL. Its binary-distribution clause is discharged by the disclaimer NOTICE renders.

harfbuzz.note: Composite, not dual: COPYING states some subdirectories carry their own COPYING, and every part binds at once.

leptonica.marker: Redistribution and use in source and binary forms
leptonica.note: No LICENSE or COPYING at its root; the terms live in leptonica-license.txt, which is why the path is recorded rather than assumed.

libjpeg.marker: The Independent JPEG Group's JPEG software
libjpeg.note: Ships no licence file at all. Its terms are the LEGAL ISSUES section of README, so README is the licence file for this component.

mujs.note: Artifex positions MuJS publicly as AGPL-or-commercial. The vendored tree grants ISC and contains no AGPL or GPL text in any file. The shipped grant governs; the path and version are recorded so a reader can check rather than dispute.

zint.spdx: BSD-3-Clause — backend only, which is all that is compiled
zint.marker: Change to BSD-license is done for backend
zint.note: The frontends and the Qt4 backend remain GPL. libzxing.vcxproj compiles 101 files, all under backend/.

zlib.marker: This software is provided 'as-is', without any express or implied
